title: Extension Access Programme
subtitle: The ministry, three counties, their projects and extension officers. Weekly. Month 9 of 24.
updated: Last updated on Wednesday 23 September at 6pm. The board only changes when something new comes in, such as a check-in, a report, a decision or a number from another system.
aim: Ministry of Agriculture. Aim: 30% more farmers get advice from an extension officer, within two years. Month 9 of 24.
whereItStands: Counties are making more visits, but few new farmers are being reached. In Kiambu, the aim changed on the way down: from more farmers to more visits.

levels.heading: What each level understood
levels.note: From the ministry down to the officers

rows.said: 30% more farmers get advice from an extension officer, within two years.

rows.flag: The meaning changed here: from more farmers to more visits.

rows.said: Buy 20 motorbikes, so officers can make more visits.
Visit registered farmers on weekdays. Many visits go to the same farmers again.
Visits are up 25%. New farmers reached are up only 8%.

counties.heading: The three counties
counties.note: Each county is its own organisation. You see summaries, never officers’ own words.

rows.why: The motorbikes are still being bought. Procurement is 3 months late.
The second payment from the county treasury has not been released.
Officers hold advice days at markets, where farmers already are.

foot.text: Nakuru is behind because money has not arrived, not because of how officers work. Kiambu is behind because the aim changed. These are not ranked.
